question: Explain whether merchandise sales changed mainly because of order volume or average merchandise per order. If sales declined, drill down by category and seller.

evidence.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-07-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-08-01') THEN o.order_id END) AS baseline_orders, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-07-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-08-01') THEN COALESCE(i.price,0) ELSE 0 END),2) AS baseline_sales, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-08-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-09-01') THEN o.order_id END) AS target_orders, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-08-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-09-01') THEN COALESCE(i.price,0) ELSE 0 END),2) AS target_sales FROM orders o LEFT JOIN order_items i ON o.order_id=i.order_id WHERE (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-07-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-08-01') OR (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-08-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-09-01')

SELECT p.product_category_name, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-08-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-09-01') THEN i.price ELSE -i.price END),2) AS delta_brl FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON i.order_id=o.order_id LEFT JOIN products p ON i.product_id=p.product_id WHERE (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-07-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-08-01') OR (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-08-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-09-01') GROUP BY p.product_category_name HAVING ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-08-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-09-01') THEN i.price ELSE -i.price END),2) < 0 ORDER BY delta_brl, p.product_category_name NULLS LAST LIMIT 5

SELECT i.seller_id AS dimension_key, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-08-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-09-01') THEN i.price ELSE -i.price END),2) AS change_value FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON i.order_id=o.order_id LEFT JOIN products p ON i.product_id=p.product_id WHERE ((o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-07-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-08-01') OR (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-08-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-09-01')) AND p.product_category_name = 'relogios_presentes' GROUP BY i.seller_id HAVING ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-08-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-09-01') THEN i.price ELSE -i.price END),2) < 0 ORDER BY change_value, i.seller_id NULLS LAST LIMIT 5

decisions.reason: Need to decompose the month-over-month merchandise sales change into order volume versus average merchandise per order to determine the main driver before any decline drill-down by category and seller.

Sales declined from 895,507.22 to 854,686.33 BRL while order volume rose slightly (6292 to 6512), so the decline is driven by lower average merchandise per order. To drill down the negative sales change as requested, rank negative category contributions.

Sales declined overall (895,507.22 -> 854,686.33) despite order volume rising (6292 -> 6512), so the decline is driven by lower average merchandise per order. The leading declining category is relogios_presentes (-23,935.53); next we drill down by ranking seller merchandise declines within that category.
